thread:
Alex: saw a weird pattern in the canary: low-latency, short streaming requests suddenly queued behind long-running streams and we hit p95 SLOs. looks like priority inversion at the gateway.
Priya: do we have per-connection priority today? we only do per-tenant bandwidth limits and a global ingress queue.
Raj: correct. long-lived streams occupy worker goroutines and block runloop slots. short requests end up waiting for a free slot.
Sasha: suggestion: admission control with 'priority tokens' per route. short requests take a cheap token; long streams acquire a heavy token pool that is sized differently.
Alex: interesting. can tokens be reclaimed if a streaming connection becomes idle (> X ms) so short calls can jump the queue?
Leo: yes - 'soft preempt' is doable: mark streams as preemptible if no chunk activity for 200ms. reclaim one token and promote queued high-priority requests.
Priya: how do we prevent abuse? clients could open many idle streams to hog tokens. we need a handshake: opt-in header + max idle windows per client.
Raj: propose explicit header `x-rw-conn-type: streaming|short` and server enforces `max_idle_per_conn = 2` and `idle_timeout_ms = 200`.
Alex: still need legacy client handling. heuristic: if client sends `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and first chunk interval > 150ms -> treat as stream and allocate heavy token. if first chunk < 150ms -> short.
Sasha: for retry interaction, hedging should be disabled for 'heavy-token' streams. but we also need a fallback path: queue-for-later (202) when heavy token pool exhausted.
Leo: agree. also add a circuit-breaker per-route that trips when queue_length > route_threshold for >30s. breaker returns 503 fast to avoid cascading.
infra-bot: alert: ingress-token-pool-pressure on route /v1/chat at 2026-02-12T15:22:10Z (auto-detected). escalation: page on-call.
Priya: config sketch:
```yaml
route: /v1/chat
admission_control:
  token_types:
    short:
      capacity: 200
      reclaim_on_idle_ms: 100
    stream:
      capacity: 30
      max_idle_per_conn: 2
      idle_timeout_ms: 200
  fallbacks:
    - when: stream.capacity_exhausted
      action: reject_or_enqueue # configured per client
  circuit_breaker:
    queue_threshold: 500
    trip_window_s: 30
    failure_response: 503
```
Raj: operational notes: metricize `tokens_in_use`, `idle_reclaims`, `preemptions`, `fallback_enqueues`. dashboards + alerting on reclaim rate > 10/s.
Sasha: SDK change: add explicit conn-type on websocket/stream creation. legacy will be heuristic. we'll add opt-in badges in the console docs.
Alex: rollout plan: feature flag `edge.priority_admission_v1`, start with low % for non-critical routes. monitor p50/p95 for short RPCs.
Priya: question on retry budget: should token consumption count against retry budget? e.g., retries also consume short tokens because they are short requests.
Leo: yes, treat retries as separate admission events and subtract tokens. but have `retry_token_reserve` so we don't starve ephemeral retries. e.g., reserve 10% of short capacity for retries.
Alex: assign owners: Priya infra + metrics, Raj gateway impl, Sasha SDK and docs, Leo tests + chaos. I'll write the brief RFC and include traffic sims.
Sasha: will prototype client header instrumenting tomorrow.
Raj: I'll spike reclaim logic and simulate 10k streams.
Alex: thanks everyone. dropping logs and flamegraphs here in case we need more context. :wave:
